newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan big bank shares unaffected by All Corp news.
newsitem.headline: Japan big bank shares unaffected by All Corp news.

text.p: Shares in major Japanese banks showed only muted reaction on Thursday to news that Tokyo-based loan firm All Corp would seek special liquidation under the weight of heavy bad loans.
Despite the news, shares in Tokai Bank Ltd, All Corp's biggest creditor bank with loans totalling 60.3 billion yen, were up 10 yen at 1,010 yen at Tokyo midday.

Shares in Sakura Bank Ltd, which has loans to the non-bank financial institution totalling 26.4 billion yen, had dropped a scant two yen to 730 yen by midday, while shares in Chuo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, another creditor bank, were up 11 yen at 845 yen.
Other major banks, such as Fuji Bank Ltd and Sumitomo Bank Ltd, were also up in morning trade.

All Corp announced earlier on Thursday that it would seek court-protected special liquidation with total debts on borrowings worth 274.5 billion yen. The special liquidation process would start in late March, it said in a statement.
The Tokyo-based non-bank said it had decided to hold a shareholders' meeting by the end of March in order to seek approval for the liquidation filing.
All Corp said that its cumulative debt exceeded its assets by 195.4 billion yen as of September 1996, and it would be hard to improve its business despite recent restructuring efforts.
The company's shares, which are registered on the over-the-counter market, were suspended for Thursday's session.
